images.caption: Figure 2:Multisource data and model overview.(a) Composition of the 47k-hour pretraining data pool. (b) Our world action model architecture, with video and action branches connected through shared masked attention.

Figure 3:World action model architecture and attention masks.(a) The video and action DiT branches are connected through shared masked attention, with text cross-attention in the video branch only. Attention masks for (b) training with clean video history under teacher forcing and (c) generating video and actions chunk by chunk at inference.

Figure 4:Multisource training data and curation pipeline.The upper panel shows representative examples from four data sources. The lower panel illustrates visual checks, action checks, format conversion, subtask segmentation, and caption generation. Captions include action descriptions at three levels of detail, along with scene and lighting information.

Figure 7:Real-world execution comparisons.Our model completes cup stacking and towel folding under the Easy setting and gift-in-box under the Hard setting, while the corresponding baseline executions fail.Light red dashed boxeshighlight the baselines’ main execution errors.
Figure 8:Generalization examples from head and external camera views.Fruit placement and rainbow stack demonstrate generalization to new objects, containers, and scene appearances.
Figure 9:Real-world evaluation layouts under Easy and Hard settings.All models use the same ten layouts for each task and setting, with three trials per layout.
Figure 10:Subtask illustrations for the three real-world tasks.
